name: Kirishima: Karakunidake from Ebino Plateau (韓国岳)
region: Kirishima-Kinkowan National Park, Miyazaki and Kagoshima
why: The highest peak of the Kirishima volcanoes, 1,700 m: a short steep climb from the Ebino plateau to a deep crater, with the cone of Takachiho and the steaming Shinmoedake to the south and on clear days Sakurajima.
book: Free. The round trip from Ebino plateau is open with Iozan at alert level 1; the old path over Iozan and the traverse to Shinmoedake (level 2, 2 km closed zone) are shut (status of 13 November 2026). The road from the Kirishima side over Iozan opens only on some weekend days: check the Ebino Eco Museum Center and the Miyazaki prefecture notices.
water: Toilets, drinks and food at the Ebino Eco Museum Center and the plateau car park only. Carry 1.5 litres.
dangers: Volcanic gas near Iozan at the start: keep to the marked path, leave if you smell sulphur strongly.
Loose scoria and rock steps on the upper slope; the crater edge has no fence.
Strong wind and fog on the summit; snow and ice from December to March.
turnaround: Fog or rain at the 5th station, or not there by 13:00: the view is gone, go back down.

points.name: Ebino plateau
points.note: About 1,200 m: the Karakunidake trailhead by the road, a few minutes from the Ebino Eco Museum Center. The path skirts the fumaroles of Iozan, then climbs through low trees.

points.name: Karakunidake 5th station
points.note: 1,520 m: out of the trees, the view opens over the plateau and its crater lakes. The steepest part is above.

points.name: Karakunidake summit crater
points.note: 1,700 m on the rim of a crater some 300 m deep. South: Onami-ike lake, Shinmoedake and Takachiho-no-mine. Return the same way.
